question: Can the non-bijective GF(2) quadratic-phase quotient evaluate first-projector signed-character sums without enumerating every affine subset, while replaying exact previously computed D4 public-law controls?
fork_classification: The signed affine first-subset enumeration in J8H is already validated on a small class, but J8J shows billions of naive first branches. A quadratic Gauss-sum quotient is a zero-new-law, reversible prerequisite to testing any broader first-record mixture. Run synthetic algebra controls, all prior exact first-mass/singleton controls, and one fixed-prefix high-variable stress fixture together; no human ranking or compute expansion is required.

hypotheses.validated_and_bounded: The exact quadratic phase identity and every stored public-law control replay within the inherited 65,536 signed-phase and 60-CPU-second caps; a high-variable fixture remains affordable as a diagnostic.
hypotheses.identity_failure: Any synthetic quadratic sum, held-out affine phase, stored first mass, or stored second singleton moment disagrees; reject the quotient as an inference method.
hypotheses.censored: The selected matrix exceeds the signed-phase or CPU ceiling, or a pinned input, public action, flux, normalization or replay gate fails; no new-law or full-prior claim is promoted.

model_boundary: R6AF ideal periodic L=2 D4 projector/fusion instrument with full-binary first public record and two fixed relation-free public actions. First-projector variables and private errors are analysis-only; the public interface and action timing are unchanged. Reuse J8I's 55 selected-first-record exact first masses and 110 complete second public laws only as validation fixtures, plus J8J's fixed same-flux coset geometry for a stress candidate.
method: For Pauli products, the sign of an ordered commuting first-projector subset plus one second operator is a GF(2) quadratic phase on each affine Z-signature preimage. Determine a particular subset and kernel basis by elimination, reconstruct the constant/linear/pair coefficients from at most 1+k+k(k-1)/2 signed products, verify held-out affine points, and sum by exact pair elimination rather than enumerating 2^k subsets. A noncommuting second operator retains the J8H exact zero rule. This is an algebraic quotient, not a map between physical public laws.

matrix.synthetic: All GF(2) quadratic forms of widths 0,1,2,3, each checked against brute-force sums.
matrix.public_controls: All 55 J8I first all-plus masses and all 55x2x22 stored second single-site expectations reconstructed from the exact complete public laws under actions [0] and [1,30,32,34,35].
matrix.stress: Enumerate only the first 256 nullspace coset masks in J8J's selected first-flux sector; select maximum number of variable first sites, tie earliest mask, then evaluate only its first all-plus signed sum. This stress value is diagnostic and not an accepted new public law.
matrix.independent_unit: One deterministic exact algebra fixture or prior stored law cell; no stochastic uncertainty.
matrix.integrity: Pin all four machine inputs and runner hash; require 55 first and 2420 singleton replays, exact public-action binding, first/second flux consistency, full-law normalization, synthetic exhaustive checks, held-out quadratic phase checks, and zero new complete-law/history/arm/bootstrap work.

acceptance: All synthetic quadratic forms and held-out affine signs pass
All 55 prior first masses and 2420 prior second singleton expectations replay exactly under unchanged actions and within cap
One deterministic high-variable stress fixture reports kernel dimension, work, CPU and diagnostic-only first mass; no uncomputed-law pooling or full-IID claim
stop_rule: Stop after the fixed matrix, or first source/action/phase/replay/integrity/65,536-phase/60-CPU-second failure. Do not expand coset prefix, calculate a new complete law or mixture, sample histories, or raise budget.
